subject: Proposal: Minimal billing payload + email backchannel for vendor activation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: minimal billing payload + email backchannel for vendor activation

Team —

Quick proposal for vendors who cannot join the portal at activation: accept a minimal CSV payload attached to a structured email backchannel instead of forcing portal onboarding. Goal is to reduce activation friction for smaller vendors while preserving PO matching and ack guarantees.

High-level idea (please skim):
- Minimal required fields: vendor_name, vendor_tax_id, invoice_number, invoice_date, amount_total, currency, purchase_order (PO number), line_count.
- Optional fields: line_items_json (compressed), vendor_email_contact, remittance_account.
- PO visibility exemption: allow a vendor-typed exemption for small consulting vendors where a single invoice may reference no PO (but must include contract reference).
- Subject token: require subject = "RBW-<vendor>-<po|contract>" so we can idempotently route.
- Ack: system will return a structured ack email (sample attached) within 5 minutes for accepted payloads and an error ack for failures.

Attachments: minimal-invoice-schema-v1.csv (sample columns) and sample-email-ack.md.

Ask:
1) Jordan — will the proposed columns map to our PO-match engine? Any columns missing that break matching?
2) Marissa — how does this fit with our vendor onboarding checklist and tax/1099 capture?
3) Vanessa — ops: how do we want to enforce subject token and rate-limit inbound SMTP?

I want to present this as a limited pilot to Keystone (they asked for a non-portal flow) and LumenMade who still send PDFs via email. If we agree, I can draft a short vendor-facing doc and a JIRA.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: minimal billing payload + email backchannel for vendor activation

Kim — thanks, this is a solid starting point. A few inline notes: 

- PO match: We can match on "purchase_order" + invoice_number. If vendors sometimes omit PO, we need a fallback: (1) contract_reference, (2) supplier_account mapping. So include contract_reference as an optional but strongly encouraged field.
- vendor_tax_id: essential for 1099/us tax reporting — Marissa will need this before go-live.
- currency: we should require ISO currency code (USD, EUR).
- line_items_json: ok as optional, but restrict size to 32KB so SMTP attachments don't blow up.
- subject token: prefer "RBW-VENDOR-<vendor_short>-<PO|CONTRACT>-YYYYMMDD" to avoid collisions. But the engine can parse both.

Operational ask: can we auto-attach the original PDF to the invoice record even if parsing fails? I think yes, but we should keep retention rules (30 days in hot storage, archive to S3).

If everyone agrees I can update the schema and add a mapping in the PO-match engine.

— Jordan
Lead, Billing Integrations

Kimberly — thanks for the proposal. A couple questions from our side as we evaluate a pilot: 

1) Subject token: if our billing system creates invoice PDFs programmatically, can we set subject to "RBW-Keystone-<PO>"? Will the portal accept multiple POs in one PDF (we sometimes batch several POs into one invoice)?
2) If we cannot produce a CSV (we generate PDFs), what is the recommended fallback? Embed a minimal CSV in the email body? Attach a one-line CSV?
3) What will the ack look like? We need an easy machine-parseable success code to reconcile on our side; sample-email-ack.md looks human-readable but we prefer JSON ack if possible.

Use-case: Keystone will likely send a single PDF per week that contains 3 POS for the same vendor. We want to ensure those map correctly and not create duplicate invoices.

If useful, I can share a redacted sample PDF and the way our system batches POs.

Thanks —
Raj Patel
Procurement Manager

Raj — thanks for the quick read and helpful detail. We ran this past engineering and ops — below is our agreed approach for a limited pilot with Keystone + LumenMade: 

Decisions (pilot scope):
- Minimal required fields to accept via email/CSV attachment: vendor_name, vendor_tax_id, invoice_number, invoice_date, amount_total, currency (ISO), purchase_order OR contract_reference, line_count.
- If batching multiple POs in a single PDF: vendors should include a CSV attachment with one row per PO/invoice (we will accept a single CSV plus the PDF). The CSV may contain multiple rows mapped to the same PDF file.
- PO visibility exemption: allowed ONLY for vendors designated as "consulting_small" in the vendor profile and only when contract_reference is provided. Ops will manually approve a short exemption list during pilot.
- Subject token: use format RBW-<vendor_short>-<PO|CONTRACT>-YYYYMMDD (e.g., RBW-KEYSTONE-PO-20270629). We will parse heuristics but ask vendors to follow format.
- Ack format: system will emit a JSON ack (machine-parseable) and a human-friendly summary. Sample JSON ack attached (sample-email-ack.md includes both).
- Retention: original PDFs kept in hot storage 30 days, then archived to cold S3.

Action items:
- Jordan: please update the PO-match mapping to accept contract_reference and a per-row CSV import.
- Marissa: confirm tax-id capture step in onboarding and whether we need vendor onboarding form change.
- Vanessa: set up inbound SMTP rate cap to 20 emails/min for the pilot and enable subject-token validation rule.
- Raj: please send one redacted sample PDF + the CSV we would attach so we can run a dry parse.

We will open ACT-445 for tracking and schedule a 30-day pilot. If the dry parse looks good we will expand.

Thanks everyone —
Kimberly Park
Senior Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference
